blocks.what_we_do: We save the first complete set of native files that you can restart from. We record its checked size.
blocks.why: The end of a module is a stable point to return to. A checkpoint is a saved copy of the analysis at one moment. Later filters can be replayed from this full copy, so we do not need to distribute every large file. A checkpoint is not evidence that anyone replicated the result.
blocks.you_need: You need the joined files from 2.7.
blocks.command:
```{r s2-8}
guided_snapshot(cfg, "2.8", guided_path(cfg, "2.7"), 2016, 296510)
check_step("2.8", data_dir = cfg$out, work_dir = cfg$out)
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

Not applicable: this step needs no PLINK command. The R code above is the complete command.

R reads the files and shows the values. It does not change the genotype files.
blocks.expected_result:
You get a full 2.8 checkpoint with 2,016 samples and 296,510 variants. The working state matches the counts and the [SHA-256](../docs/glossary.md#sha-256) checks of its checkpoint. A SHA-256 check compares a short fingerprint of a file, to prove that the file has not changed.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks and the expected counts passed on Windows.
blocks.troubleshooting: Stop at the first error message. Check the input file named in the message. Check that the previous step finished. Keep the command and the console output (the text printed in R). Do not use files from a different version of the dataset. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).
